explanation: A body whose one row names a parameter is a callable alias of whatever callable the parameter receives: inside `Use(f)`, `A = f` makes `A(9)`, `2.A` and `Apply(A, 4)` call the supplied `Square` with exactly those new arguments. When the parameter receives a plain value, `A` is just that value — bare `A` and `A()` read it without rerunning anything — so `A(1)` is an arity error, and a passed `A` is no callable.

explanation: `A = R.Algorithm` names the captured call's callee, so `A` is an alias of it: `A(9)` is a fresh call with the new argument, `[1, 2].map(A)` uses it as a callback, and an alias of `A` (`B = A`, also declared before its target) is the same callable. Written bare, `A` is the callee read as a value.

`A = b.G` is a member reference: its head `b` is a parameter, so `G` is a member name, never an input of `A`. `Use(Box)` calls `Box.G(3)`, the `G` that `b` declares, never the lexical `G`. On a receiver that lacks `G`, `b.G` is the computed value `G(b)`: `A` then names that value, so calling it with an argument is an arity error.

`A = f` is a runtime REFERENCE to whatever `f` receives, so every observation of `A` is that target's: passing it (`Navigate(A)`) and writing `A.K` both read `Lib`'s own member `K` (99). A definition written in braces is a structure of its own instead: `{ public K = 5 ⏎ f }` reads its own `K`.
notes: M4★ (ALIAS-UNIFY-1, October 2026): formerly written `A.K` on the alias took the fallback `K(A)` (7).

explanation: A structure whose one row names a parameter is still a namespace of its own declarations: `open Lib` imports `X`, and the bare `Lib` reads the parameter's value.
Calling `A = R.Algorithm` needs `R`'s call reference; `R = 5` is not one, so the call reports that type mismatch instead of treating `A` as an ordinary property.

Capture(meta op) = op
A = R.Algorithm
R = Capture(A(1))

A(2)
explanation: `A` needs `R`'s callee, and `R` captures a call of `A` itself, so resolving `A` re-enters its own resolution: a demand cycle, never a loop.

`A = b.G` names what `b.G` gives in this call of `F`, and it is worked out once per call: the path `B.A` and the read of `B` (whose row reads `A`) use the same `A`, so `tick()` runs once. An alias is worked out exactly as often as the same line written as an ordinary property (`P = b.G + 0`) would be.
notes: ALIAS-CELL-LIFETIME (November 2026): formerly (1, 2) — the read of `B` minted an activation of its own, and with it a second cell for `A` in the same call of `F`.

explanation: Reading `B` or `B.A` uses the `A` of this call of `F`, however often and in whatever order. Only the explicit call `B()` runs `B`'s body afresh, with an `A` of its own (the second `tick()`); the `B.A` after it reads the first one again. `A` depends on `b`, so it belongs to one call, exactly like a property that reads `b`.

    A(1), A(2), A(3)

Ten(x) = x * 10
Hun(x) = x * 100
Pick(n) = if(n == 1, Cap(Ten(0)), Cap(Hun(0)))
Outer(k) = {
    A = Pick(tick() + k).Algorithm
    A(1)
}
Outer(0)
Outer(0)

Cap(meta r) = r
Ten(x) = x * 10
Hun(x) = x * 100
Pick(n) = if(n == 1, Cap(Ten(0)), Cap(Hun(0)))
Outer(k) = {
    P = Pick(tick() + k)
    P.Algorithm(1)
}
Outer(0)
Outer(0)

explanation: `A = Pick(tick()).Algorithm` is declared inside `Outer`, so every call of `Outer` works out its own `A`: the first call's `tick()` is 1 and picks `Ten`, the second call's is 2 and picks `Hun`. It makes no difference that the line uses nothing the call supplies. Inside one call `A` is worked out once, however often it is used — exactly as the property `P = Pick(tick())` is.
notes: INNER-PROPERTY LIFETIME (November 2026): every call of the owner has a fresh alias, whether or not its line uses the call's input. Under ALIAS-CELL-LIFETIME alone (from 2026-11-15) this was (10, 10) — one cell for the run, because `A`'s line reads nothing of the call; before that (10, 100), by an activation key that an unused neighbour could change (the next case).

explanation: An unused neighbour never changes what a program gives. `U = k + 0` reads `F`'s input and is never used. Each explicit call `Outer()` is a call of `Outer` and works out its own `A` — the first picks `Ten`, the second `Hun` — with or without `U`.
notes: ALIAS-CELL-LIFETIME (November 2026) made this program and its twin without `U` agree (formerly (10, 100) with `U` and (10, 10) without it); they agreed on (10, 10) until INNER-PROPERTY LIFETIME (November 2026), under which each explicit call of `Outer` has its own `A`: (10, 100) for both.

Outer.A(1)
Outer(0)
Outer.A(1)

explanation: `Outer(0)` works out the `A` of that call (`tick()` is 1: `Ten`). `Outer.A(1)` is written outside every call of `Outer`, so it uses the `A` that belongs to the run, worked out separately (`tick()` is 2: `Hun`). The order does not matter, and every read from outside uses that same one: a call of `Outer` never supplies it and never replaces it.
notes: INNER-PROPERTY LIFETIME (November 2026): the read from outside every call of the owner has its own alias, apart from every call's. Under ALIAS-CELL-LIFETIME alone (from 2026-11-15) this was (10, 10) — one cell for the run, shared by the call and the outside read.
